doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: What captivated her about hearing Charlie Parker
summary: Four notes of Bird raised the hair on her arm and she dedicated her life to the music; Bird later became like a big brother.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now if we go back to when you first heard Charlie Parker, what made it so distinctive or different than the music you had been listening to? What was it that captivated you about Charlie Parker?

Oh. His heart and soul and this whole thing. I mean, it just hit me. I heard four notes and the hair was standing up on my arm. On my head, too, I guess. I mean, I, I said, “Oh, my God. That‟s it! That‟s it! That‟s what I want to do.” And that‟s why I said, the dedication at that

early age… I made a dedication to make this music my life, as I said, regardless of how I got it out there, you know. So I mean, just sitting here today with this tremendous honor, you know. Who would ever thought that? I never expected it. I really didn‟t. So it was Bird. It‟s all Bird‟s fault. [laughs] Blame it on the Bird!
Blame it on the Bird. Oh, he was wonderful, you know. And I‟ll get into that later. He became like a big brother to me.
